subject: Yoruba
examFormat: Two papers; rubrics are written in Yoruba. Paper 1 has 60 multiple-choice questions (Language 30, Literature 22, Culture 8) answered in 1 hour for 60 marks. Paper 2 is essay-type in three sections (Language, Literature, Culture), 2 hours for 100 marks: six questions in all (three from Section A, two from Section B, one from Section C), answered in Yoruba using the official orthography and metalanguage. Paper 1 content is the same as Paper 2.
excluded: Selected texts for 2014-2015 and reference lists (set books change; described generically).

topics.name: Composition (Yoruba)
topics.content: Candidates are advised to write about 300 words and spend not more than 45 minutes on this section. The essay will be any of the listed types: narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue, debate, letter writing.

topics.name: Sound System (Yoruba)
objectives: Explain the production of vowels, consonants and syllabic nasal in terms of place and manner
Classify vowels, consonants and syllabic nasal phonetically and phonemically
Explain sound processes, e.g. vowel harmony, assimilation, elision
Describe the sound system aspect of the orthography
topics.content: Candidates answer one question from the two set.

topics.name: Grammar (Yoruba)
objectives: Explain word structure and word formation
Identify word classes: nouns, verbs, adverbs, pronouns, adjectives, etc.
Explain grammatical categories: subject, object, complement, predicate, number, person, tense, aspect, mood, etc.
Describe the structure and type of sentences
topics.content: Candidates answer one question from the two made available.

topics.name: Oral Literature (Yoruba)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on oral prose, poetry and drama
topics.content: In Oral Literature there are three set books covering prose, poetry and drama; one question is set on each and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Written Literature (Yoruba)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on written prose, poetry and drama
topics.content: In Written Literature there are three set books covering prose, poetry and drama; one question is set on each and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Customs (Yoruba)
objectives: Describe home training: greetings, respect for superiors, cleanliness, tolerance, integrity, hard work, etc.
Describe funerals: traditional and modern methods
Describe inheritance: traditional and modern methods
topics.content: Two questions are set on customs and institutions and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Institutions (Yoruba)
objectives: Describe politics: family structure, age grades, chieftaincy, Obaship, etc.
Explain Yoruba beliefs about Olodumare (God), deities/divinities, other invisible forces, etc.
Describe modern religions: Islam, Christianity, etc.
Describe the economy: adverts, money lending, cooperative efforts, etc.
topics.content: Two questions are set on customs and institutions and candidates answer any one.
